question: RULE on E4 (DRC-4037). Three asks. FIRST, approve the delivery split: a documentation-only groundwork issue delivering docs/plans/git-probe-security-scope.md, with E4 blocked on it — the exact DRC-4061 and DRC-4177 shape, verified at both ends by commit (plan doc added in its own PR, then promoted into SECURITY.md and deleted by the implementation PR). SECOND, amend two of the four bounds you ruled on 2026-08-28, because triage measured that they cannot deliver their own intent as written: bound 3 names finished_at, which is a turn-stop stamp that re-arms every turn and would make the one-shot into a per-turn poll — the exact thing bound 3 forbids — so build to session_ended instead; and bound 2 fixes a non-nullable dirty flag, which would publish a confident false for the majority of rows that can never be probed, so read it as nullable with None meaning not probed. THIRD, strike E4 own sentence that a PR carrying both the amendment and the runtime change does not satisfy it, which is absent from DEC-3 outcome and forbids exactly what DEC-1 and DEC-2 implementation PRs did. Approving authorizes the Linear writes and makes the groundwork issue the next pick.

artifacts.summary: E4 is buildable, and the question that decided it answers better than the issue expected. The absolute working directory survives: Event.cwd (events.py:167, bounded 4096, oversized values dropped rather than truncated) already carries it on the very event the probe should fire from, and the real SessionEnd captures for Claude and Droid both carry cwd — so the retention cost is zero rather than the small new retention the issue assumed. Seven claims were re-derived at v0.18.0 (ef425b2, not the v0.17.1 the dispatch stated); two were refuted, one refined, the rest hold. The two refutations are both about bounds the captain already ruled. Bound 3 names finished_at, which _mark_finished writes on every idle overlay and pops on every working overlay (observation.py:354-376, 360-362), so a probe hung there fires once per turn stop — forty turns, forty subprocesses inside the user repository, which is a poll with extra steps and the exact thing bound 3 exists to forbid. The genuine one-shot edge is session_ended, which E2 deliberately excluded from that stamp. Bound 3 property survives; its named artifact cannot deliver it. Bound 2 fixes the surface at a non-nullable dirty bool, but six of ten harnesses have no event adapter and can never emit session_ended, and adding --no-git, a non-repository directory and git absent from PATH means most rows will never be probed — so a non-nullable flag publishes a confident clean over no evidence. The product already has the precedent and states it: finished_at None means no stop observed and never did not finish, and acquisition exists to disclose unknowability rather than hide it. On the hazards, the flags are now stronger evidence than DEC-3 had: four fresh probe repositories from an identical racy-clean state show plain rewrites .git/index AND runs the script, --no-optional-locks alone stops the write only, -c core.fsmonitor= alone stops the script only, both stop both — so neither flag can be dropped. One DEC-3 figure did not reproduce and should not be repeated in the amendment: the fsmonitor script ran once, not twice, at git 2.55.0; the security consequence is unchanged. Also corrected: the index write is race resolution rather than an unconditional per-invocation write, and changed counts porcelain entries rather than files, so one modified file plus five untracked in one new directory measures as 2. Seven acceptance criteria, six offline and one interactive, each Verified by naming a test file:line, a capture, or a live drive. The stale DEC-3 milestone passage is drafted as dated rather than corrected. Nothing was written to Linear and no repository file changed.
